purpose: Decide which part of The Graph serves a data need, without guessing. Evaluate rules in order; first match wins.

inputs.chain: network id as used in chains.json (registry ids, e.g. 'mainnet','base','matic','arbitrum-one')
inputs.goal: one of: balances | transfers | dex | nft | markets | protocol_state | own_contract | bulk
inputs.contract: optional lowercase 0x address; if given, look it up in contracts.json FIRST

preflight.do: If a contract address is given, look it up in contracts.json.
preflight.onHit: If the entry has subgraphIds, that contract is already indexed: use catalog.json and stop. If it only has a protocol + token-api source, the protocol is decoded by Token API: query by protocol, do not index.
preflight.onMiss: Absence is NOT proof nothing indexes it. contracts.json covers DEX factories plus catalogued protocols only. Fall through to the rules, and tell the user to check thegraph.com/explorer.

preflight.do: Look up the chain in chains.json to read its services: sg (subgraphs), ss (substreams), fh (firehose), tapi (Token API).

then.why: Polymarket and Hyperliquid are indexed as first-class datasets with OI, positions and PnL precomputed; they are dataset-scoped, not chain-scoped.
then.keyNote: market lookup is open; per-user positions need a thegraph.market Bearer token

then.why: Full-chain scans and backfills replay in parallel; a subgraph makes a single sequential pass.
No Substreams or Firehose endpoint on this network; parallel replay is unavailable.
Token-shaped data on a Token API chain needs no indexing at all — it is a REST call.
then.caveat: The /v1/evm/nft/* family is EVM-only; Solana NFTs need a subgraph or Substreams.

then.why: Token API covers only 10 networks. Check catalog.json for this chain before building.
Your own contract is the one case where nothing can already exist.
then.checkFirst: If you forked a known factory, look the factory address up in contracts.json first.

then.why: This network has no subgraph deploy endpoint.
A verified subgraph already serves this chain; every catalog.json entry carries a query that was actually executed.
then.use: catalog.json — filter by chain, sort by queryFeesGrt descending, and READ fieldWarning before trusting any field.

then.why: Nothing in this catalogue covers it, and the chain supports subgraphs. The catalogue is a verified sample, not the whole network — search the Explorer first.

hardEarnedWarnings.rule: Never use as an orderBy. Verified live: ranking by it returns untracked scam pairs reporting ~8.8e33 USD with volumeUSD=0. Rank by trackedReserveETH instead; reserveUSD is fine to READ on an already-selected pair.
Do not use as an orderBy — inflated by illiquid spam-token pools, so the top row is often a dead pool with volumeUSD=0. Rank by volumeUSD.
Mirrors totalDepositBalanceUSD exactly; it is NOT net of borrows. Do not sum it alongside borrow totals.
Historically wrong by ~1e6 and worse. Do not serve it without an explicit warning.

Query _meta { block { number } } FIRST, every time. Lifetime query fees are historical and say nothing about current health: on 2026-09-14 one catalogued subgraph with ~31,675 GRT in fees returned no data to our probe. Test before you rely — do not treat this catalogue, or fees, as a health check.

keys.name: The Graph Market token
keys.free: open endpoints need no key at all

testingStance.weDoNotCertify: This dataset reports existence and a single point-in-time observation. It does not certify that any endpoint works now.
testingStance.alwaysDo: Run { _meta { block { number } } } against a subgraph before trusting it, and compare to the chain head.
testingStance.why: Query fees are lifetime and historical. A subgraph with six figures of fees can still return nothing today — we observed exactly that once while building this.
